name: Bright terracotta
lede: Bright terracotta is a strong coral-red whose Japanese library name, Jinzamomi, means "thrice-dyed crimson," and it sits under 5 units from plain [[terracotta]].

sections.title: Jinzamomi, dyed three times
sections.body:
The Wikipedia survey "Traditional colors of Japan" lists this color under the romanized name Jinzamomi, written 甚三紅 [1]. The library glosses the kanji as "thrice-dyed crimson": a dye bath repeated to deepen the red, rather than a single quick dip [1]. No book consulted here independently confirms a date, dyer, or dyestuff, so the craft detail behind the gloss is undocumented [1].

The nearest already-named color in our library is [[terracotta]], at a color-distance of 4.8 by the CIEDE2000 formula, and the library also lists [[grapefruit]] as a close neighbor [1]. The hex given here, #F7665A, is a modern screen approximation fit to that gloss, not a measurement of any dyed cloth [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
A color within range of this swatch appears in 11 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive by the painting-level count, about 0.05 percent; the within-painting lens, which can count a color more than once per canvas, finds it 15 times, as photographed [2]. That makes it rarer than 64 percent of the named colors we track [2].

It peaks mildly in the 1800s, present in 6 of 8,345 paintings from that century, close to the expected rate [2]. Inside the paintings that carry it, it plays only one role: an accent, never a dominant field or a shadow [2].
